about: Chrome extension (MV3) that highlights broken links: a service worker, a content script per tab, a popup; built with Vite

rules.text: The extension's service worker holds no state between events; everything it needs is read from chrome.storage.local when an event arrives and written back before the handler returns
The popup never touches the page itself; it sends a message to the service worker, which forwards it to the content script of the active tab and relays the reply
Never add a permission to manifest.json without an issue that says why it is needed; the store review flags every added permission

about: Go CLI that tags audio files: scan builds a plan file, apply writes the tags from it; taglib through cgo

rules.text: scan is read-only by design: it walks the folders, builds the plan, prints it and writes nothing; tags change only when apply is run with that plan file
The cache under ~/.cache/tinwhistle is keyed by the file's size and mtime; a miss recomputes, and the cache is never needed for a correct result, only for speed
Never commit the audio fixtures under test/audio/large/; they are fetched by the test script from the bucket

about: NestJS payments API over Postgres behind an Envoy gateway; each service owns its schema; events through an outbox table and a relay

rules.text: The rate limiter sits in the gateway and counts per API key in Redis with a sliding window; the services behind it never see a request over the limit and have no limiter of their own
A service writes each event into its own outbox table inside the transaction that made the change and the relay publishes from there; nothing publishes to the broker directly
A merged migration is never edited; every schema change is a new numbered file under migrations/

about: Python static site generator: content/ in Markdown, templates/ in Jinja, rendered partials cached in .cache/ by content hash, output in dist/

rules.text: dist/ is wiped and rebuilt on every build, which is why nothing in dist/ is ever edited by hand: an edit there would not survive the next build
The dev server watches content/ and templates/, rebuilds only the pages whose inputs changed and pushes a reload over a websocket; it never writes to dist/ itself, the build does
Never add a runtime dependency without a line in DECISIONS.md saying why

about: Rust service that runs cron-style jobs from a Postgres table, one scheduler per replica with a leader lease

rules.text: Every job run is idempotent by construction: the run id is derived from the job id and the scheduled time, so a retry after a crash reuses the id and the store rejects a second insert; no job can run twice for one slot
The scheduler reads the clock once per tick from the database with now(), never from the host, so every replica agrees on the time
Never run the scheduler binary against the shared staging database from a laptop; local runs use the Docker Postgres

about: Tauri desktop notes app: a Svelte front end, a Rust core with SQLite, a sync engine to the user's own WebDAV; notes are Markdown files on disk

rules.text: The app writes every change to the local SQLite first and the sync engine pushes diffs later; the UI never waits on the network, and offline is the normal state with the push queued
Each plugin runs in its own worker with a message channel and no filesystem access of its own; a plugin asks the host for a file over the channel and the host decides
Never edit the generated bindings under src/bindings/; change the Rust types and run cargo run --bin gen-bindings
